samples.summary: New `folderId` path on PATCH /documents/:id has no DTO validation — a non-string value reaches Prisma and 500s
samples.evidence: `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }` is an inline type, so the global `ValidationPipe` (main.ts:66, whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted) skips it entirely (metatype is `Object`). A body like `{"folderId": 5}` or `{"folderId": {}}` passes `body.folderId !== undefined` and `!== null`, then reaches `folderService.assertSameWorkspace(body.folderId, workspaceId)` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({ where: { id: 5 } })`, which raises `PrismaClientValidationError` and surfaces as a 500 instead of a 400. The sibling folders surface added in this same change uses `UpdateFolderDto` (`@IsUUID()`) precisely for this; the documents surface does not. Note the same is true for an unexpected extra field: it is now silently dropped from `data` rather than rejected.
searchedFor: grep for a DTO used by api/v1 documents controller

samples.summary: `folders delete` help text tells the user only that documents survive; it omits that all descendant folders are permanently deleted
samples.evidence: The description reads 'Delete a folder; its documents return to the workspace root (never deleted)'. Per `Folder_parentId_fkey ... ON DELETE CASCADE` (packages/backend/prisma/migrations/20260719142600_add_workspace_folders/migration.sql:29) the delete also destroys every descendant folder — which the schema registry entry does say ('Delete a folder and its descendant folders'). The CLI help, which is what an operator or agent reads immediately before running a destructive command, states the reassuring half only, so a subtree delete can be issued believing it removes one folder.

samples.summary: `folders create --parent ''` silently creates at the workspace root instead of failing
samples.evidence: `const { parent } = this.opts(); ... if (parent) body.parentId = parent;` and `HttpClient.createFolder` likewise does `if (parentId) body.parentId = parentId`. An explicitly supplied but empty `--parent ''` is therefore dropped client-side and the folder is created at the root, reported as success — the server would have rejected it (`@IsUUID()` fails on `''`). Every other id in this CLI goes through `seg()`, which refuses the empty segment for exactly this reason (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:32). The backend's `if (body.parentId)` in folders.controller.ts:92 has the same truthiness gap, so an empty parentId that did reach it would skip `assertSameWorkspace` too.

samples.summary: `assertNoCycle` is a non-transactional read-then-write; two concurrent moves can still commit a cycle, and this change adds a second concurrent surface
samples.evidence: `assertNoCycle` walks the parent chain with separate `findUnique` calls and the subsequent `folderService.update` is not in the same transaction or under any lock. Two simultaneous moves (A under B, B under A) can each pass the check and both commit, leaving a cycle in `Folder.parentId`. `assertNoCycle` itself has a `visited` guard so it will not loop afterwards, but any consumer that reconstructs the tree from the flat list (the documented use of `parentId` in the new `folders list`) has no such protection. The defect is pre-existing in folder.controller.ts:100, but this change makes folder moves reachable from a second, scriptable surface (API keys via `ApiV1FoldersController.update`), which is where concurrent automated moves become likely.

samples.summary: `docs move <doc-id>` with the optional folder argument forgotten silently relocates the document to the workspace root
samples.evidence: `const target = folderId ?? null;` turns an omitted positional into an explicit `null`, which the backend treats as `folder: { disconnect: true }` (documents.controller.ts:141). A caller who mistypes or forgets the destination (`wafflebase docs move <id>` instead of `... <id> <folder>`) gets a successful, unconfirmed move out of whatever folder the document was filed in, with no way to learn the previous folder from the response. `folders move <folder-id>` has the identical shape. The behaviour is deliberate per the comments, but there is no confirmation flag or distinct `--root` spelling separating 'move to root' from 'argument missing'.
